On 1998-02-01 esjeje1@aol.com(Esjeje1) said:
 es>If you revisit paragraph 196, "...It will be easier to destroy the
 es>industrial system on a worldwide basis if the world economy is so
 es>unified that its breakdown in any one major nation will lead to its
 es>breakdown in all industrialized nations."
 es>Enter the IMF, with its goal of stabalizing industrial economies.
 es>Congress is about to debate funding the IMF with an additional $20
 es>Billion US dollars. The mainstream reporting is that if this isn't
 es>done, the effects of collapses in other countries who are both our
 es>customers and our competitors would damage our own economy. Various
 es>groups want to attach provisions to any US IMF fundings -
 es>environmental policies, labor or human rights provisions, and other
 es>groups, though of course, those which will be taken most seriously
 es>are the economic interests. The corporate world is quite anxious
 es>that the IMF funding be passed through Congress. Interesting enough,
 es>several Congressmen are not willing, due to the above mentioned
 es>concerns. (I don't have their names, I just listen to NPR, which I
 es>personally find to be the least biased source of news, when I feel
 es>like listening to news at all.) Meanwhile, I seem to have read
 es>somewhere that the Pope is encouraging poor third world countries
 es>not to repay their IMF loans (which actually serve to cripple those
 es>countries more, due to the large interest payments, and which cause
 es>environmental degradation amongst other things.) The Pope is also
 es>critical not only of communism, but of capitalism - he's not too
 es>happy with what's going on in Poland. If anyone has more info on
 es>these subjects, I would be interested.
 es>Couple this with the "Year 2000" problem (and recently, the
 es>Washington Post reported that there is a serious lack of
 es>programmers. I imagine there is a lack of COBOL or other "legacy"
 es>(old programming languages) programmers to solve this problem,
 es>which supposedly will bring down government, banking and other
 es>industry systems.) The Year 2000 problem will start affecting
 es>people before the year 2000, because the fiscal year will start in
 es>1999. So, I am wondering, what is everyone on this newsgroup
 es>prepared to do? I would welcome the collapse of the IMF, because I
 es>think it is a ruthless organization. We can't predict the outcome
 es>of its collapse though.
 es>This is just the sort of breakdown discussed in the "manifesto".
 es>The members of this newsgroup have certainly represented the ideals
 es>in paragraph 187 "On the more sophisticated level, the ideology
 es>should address itself to people who are intelligent, thoughtful and
 es>rational. The object should be to create a core of people who will
 es>be opposed to the industrial system on a rational, thought-out
 es>basis, with full appreciation of the problems and ambiguities
 es>involved, and of the price that has to be paid for getting rid of
 es>the system. It is particularly important to attract people of this
 es>type, as they are capable people and will be instrumental in
 es>influencing others." I know I have done my small part in spreading
 es>the message, and will continue to do so.
 es>So, now we have a chance to make a difference. The future predicted
 es>in Ted's work may be closer than we thought. His work was quite
 es>timely indeed. Perhaps a little too close shaved for some.
 es>What are we going to do about it?
 es>Esjeje1@aol.com
 es>"Nobody told me there'd be days like these; strange days indeed..."
 es>John Lennon
